newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali chief vows doctor's killers will be caught.
newsitem.headline: Somali chief vows doctor's killers will be caught.

text.p: Somali faction leader Hussein Aideed promised on Tuesday that the killers of a Portuguese doctor shot dead in a hospital in the southern town of Baidoa would be caught.
In a speech marking Somalia's 37th anniversary of independence, Aideed said the killing of aid workers damaged the peace process and international efforts to help the Somali people.
"I promise those behind the killing of Dr Rocardo Marques will be apprehended," Aideed told thousands of people at a stadium in southern Mogadishu, the faction leader's power base.

Marques, 35, who worked for the international medical agency Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF) (Doctors without Frontiers), was shot dead on June 20 in a hospital in Baidoa controlled by Aideed's forces. Seven aid workers were evacuated from the town after the murder.
Somalia has had no central government since the fall of late dictator Siad Barre in 1991. Rival faction leaders then turned their guns on each other, fuelling a famine that killed 300,000 people.
Aid agencies have demanded Aideed and other faction leaders live up to their promises to safeguard foreign aid workers in the Horn of Africa country before aid operations are increased.
Independence Day celebrations in north Mogadishu were marred by the assassination of a member of the central committee of faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed's coalition.

Abdullahi Haji Mohamed Afjirib was gunned down by three men wearing masks and firing assault rifles as he sat at a cafe drinking coffee, witnesses said. Two other people were killed and one was wounded.
Aideed was elected president by supporters in August last year following the death of his father, Mohamed Farah Aideed.
Ali Mahdi, who is based in north Mogadishu and also claims the title of president, and his allies refuse to accept Aideed's rule.
